newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair slams MP for aiding Adams book launch.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair slams MP for aiding Adams book launch.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair on Monday condemned one of his own Labour members of parliament for hosting the launch of Irish Republican Gerry Adams's autobiography at the House of Commons.

"I condemn this event without reservation and totally dissociate the Labour Party from it," Blair said of the book launch by the leader of Sinn Fein, political wing of the Irish Republican Army fighting to oust Britain from Northern Ireland.
Blair's angry comment came after Labour parliamentarian Jeremy Corbyn booked a committee room in parliament for the September 26 launch.
Adams was member of parliament for West Belfast from 1983-1992 but he never took up his seat and did not swear the oath of allegiance to Britain's Queen Elizabeth.
Adams's book, "Before the Dawn", has already sparked controversy after extracts were published as a short story, describing a gunman's justification for shooting a British soldier.
Under parliamentary rules, Adams is entitled as a former member to use a parliamentary room as long as it is booked by a sitting member.
